top_categories.workout_context: 18,045ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
128ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Otztaler Radmarathon, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
At mile 60 of 141, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Otztaler Radmarathon's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before August.
18,045ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Otztaler Radmarathon. Train it until it feels boring.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 141 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.

Road-specific control matters at Otztaler Radmarathon. Practice on paved Alpine mountain passes: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 141 miles.
Low-cadence force work supports 18,045ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 18,045ft of climbing on paved Alpine mountain passes does to your power file on race day.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on paved Alpine mountain passes can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

race_overlay.weather: August in Solden, Otztal Valley, Tyrol, Austria — Late August in the high Austrian/Italian Alps delivers a full spectrum of conditions in a single day. The 6:30 AM start in Solden is cold (5-10C). Valley sections warm rapidly through the day (20-30C). The Timmelsjoch at 2,474m can approach freezing with severe wind chill, even in August. The route crosses the main Alpine ridge twice, exposing riders to weather changes from north to south slope. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks, including rain protection and wet-road braking, and practice stable positioning in crosswinds before Otztaler Radmarathon. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Otztaler Radmarathon’s 141 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Otztaler Radmarathon includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing. Timmelsjoch summit at 2,474m: wind chill can bring effective temperature below freezing; 30+ km of climbing to the Timmelsjoch means prolonged cold exposure at altitude.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, TT Threshold, and Over Under to prepare you for 141 miles of paved alpine mountain passes in Solden, Otztal Valley, Tyrol, Austria.
